feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital/communications CV with clear positioning, credible scope, and relevant public-sector leadership experience. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies that reduce sharpness and impact.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear executive profile: the headline and summary position you well as a digital platform and communications leader with a strong niche in public-sector modernization.  
- Credible experience progression: long tenure at NACo shows advancement, increasing responsibility, and leadership across web, analytics, governance, and multimedia.  
- Good use of scale indicators: metrics like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers” strengthen impact and credibility.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition and tighten structure: “digital,” “platform,” “governance,” and similar themes recur across summary, competencies, skills, and experience. Consolidate overlapping sections like Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results. Include measurable improvements in traffic, engagement, efficiency, adoption, or cost savings where possible.  
- Fix stylistic inconsistencies: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation around list bullets is inconsistent; “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly; “Ranked among the top public universities…” under Education adds little value.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning that aligns well with the experience section, but it’s slightly dense and repeats several ideas already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and skills sections. Tightening it and adding one concrete scale cue would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms” with stronger, more direct verbs like “leading” or “modernizing.”
- Add a concrete scale marker from recent roles, e.g. “10,000+ page websites” or “3.5M annual page views.”
- Trim the list of capabilities to the most differentiating themes: web modernization, governance, analytics, and AI-enabled experiences.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing public-sector web platforms, governance models, and content operations for high-volume communications. Leads enterprise website transformation, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, and AI-enabled content experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; consider narrowing to “AI-enabled content experiences.”
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” closely echoes the subtitle and skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this section largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It will be more effective if tightened, made more parallel in style, and focused on differentiating strengths rather than restating broad categories.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, more scannable noun phrases with consistent structure and fewer filler words.
- Prioritize highest-value, recent strengths tied to target roles: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, automation, and multimedia.
- Consider this rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- Replace “content experiences” with “content discovery” or “user experience” for clearer meaning.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with Topline Skills and multiple NACo roles.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” is already well covered in Work Experience and Technical + IT.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the footer currently repeats achievements already covered in Work Experience and reads a bit dense. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing distinct outcomes or formats will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short lead-in like “Selected Recent Projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use consistent action/result structure: “Built/Developed [thing] using [methods/features] to [outcome].”
- Tighten wording: change “Designed an AI-enabled…” to “Built an AI-enabled…” for stronger execution language; hyphenate “bill-level” consistently.
- Consider this cleaner version: “AI Hybrid Search: Built an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search, and bill-level chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series overlap with the current freelance and NACo bullets; keep the footer only if framed as selected examples, not a repeat of responsibilities.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” may need a clearer name or context if the employer/project is not obvious elsewhere.

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Website

items.title: Core Competencies

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and project footer. Make it sharper by emphasizing scope, outcomes, and the most senior/technical contributions.

Suggested edit
- Open with a tighter lead: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, content operations, and campaign delivery.”
- Consolidate bullets around 4 themes: enterprise systems/analytics, Drupal campaign builds, governance across channels, and AI-enabled search.
- Add measurable scope where possible: number of sites/pages/users, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, publishing teams supported, or efficiency gains.
- Use stronger outcome phrasing, e.g. “Built Drupal microsites and modular storytelling components that improved campaign launch speed and reusable content publishing” and “Led AI-enabled search strategy spanning retrieval design, structured content, and discovery UX.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item overlaps with the footer project summaries; keep project names/details there and focus this entry on role-level impact.
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” repeats the headline/profile language; quantify or specify what changed.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground enterprise outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the strongest achievements into sharper, outcome-led bullets: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page Drupal website, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel oversight more strategic and measurable: replace “Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels…” with impact such as audience growth, engagement, send volume, or campaign performance if available.
- Tighten ops bullets: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio…” and “Expanded analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving executive reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Email/social/video management” overlaps with Associate Communications Director; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, modernization, and systems.
- Video-program language overlaps with older NACo roles and Recent Projects; emphasize studio build-out and organizational capacity here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Make it more specific to executional leadership and channel growth during 2018–2022, with clearer outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, improving editorial coordination and advocacy delivery.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Add measurable impact if available: newsletter open/click growth, video views, publishing volume, turnaround time, or stakeholder adoption.
- Rephrase for stronger ownership: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel” and “Built cross-team editorial planning processes linking communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Improved digital publishing workflows” overlaps with the Director role’s governance/standards language; specify what changed here operationally.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; frame this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize leadership-level strengths not already repeated elsewhere, and make the phrasing more distinctive and outcome-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, executive-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy & campaign planning
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “communications” to better match the rest of the CV and avoid sounding purely copy-focused.
- Keep parallel structure: all noun phrases, no mixed styles.
- If space allows, add one differentiator such as “AI-enabled content discovery strategy” to reflect recent work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” closely duplicate Core Competencies and the header.
- “Audience-focused content planning” overlaps with campaign/storytelling language in recent project and consulting entries.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a generic tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills item, make it more selective, grouped, and tied to the candidate’s recent Drupal/CMS modernization and AI-search work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as grouped capabilities, not a long list: “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint & Power Pages • CMS modernization & front-end implementation • API integrations & workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Remove lower-signal basics like “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” from this topline section; keep those in “Technical + IT.”
- Prioritize recent, differentiating strengths first: put “Drupal,” “CMS modernization,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” at the front.
- If space allows, sharpen phrasing to outcomes-oriented language: “Enterprise CMS modernization” or “Platform integration & workflow automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and reserve detailed tools for the technical section.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies and the header summary.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for a senior digital leader, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize decision-making and business impact.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to outcomes-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting and optimization” rather than just platform names.
- Tighten and group related items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” then “KPI frameworks, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Consider stronger phrasing: replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboards and decision support.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy and optimization • KPI framework design • Executive dashboards and decision support • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • SEO and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates the “Data, Analytics & Optimization” list in Technical + IT; keep this section more strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full tool inventory.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrasing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize delivery capability and recent leadership-level multimedia work rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools/tasks to outcomes and scope: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production workflows”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a stronger, broader phrase like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end video production”
- Consider adding scale/context if true: “for advocacy, executive communications, and member-facing events”
- Keep to 4 bullets max and avoid software/tool detail here since Premiere Pro, Audition, etc. already appear elsewhere

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” overlaps with Core Competencies (“Multimedia production and livestream operations”); use distinct wording like “livestream and hybrid event delivery”
- “PTZ camera systems” is very tool-specific for a topline section; better placed under Technical + IT if retained

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent CMS expertise or differentiated by proficiency/context.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance and recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector focus) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**.
- Add light qualifiers to show depth without turning it into a sentence: **Drupal (migration, microsites, governance)** • **WordPress** • **SharePoint** • **Power Pages** • **GitHub Pages**.
- If space allows, split by strength: **Primary:** Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint | **Working knowledge:** Power Pages, GitHub Pages.
- Keep this item platform-only; save implementation detail for the coding/technical line.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one instance or making this version more proficiency-based.
- “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere, so don’t repeat that phrase here.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, and automation work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename/refocus to: “Front-End & Technical Implementation”
- Rewrite as: “HTML5/CSS3 • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions/CI workflows”
- Drop version numbers unless required; “HTML/CSS” is cleaner and more current.
- If accurate, add one proof point in nearby experience instead of here, e.g., “implemented front-end fixes, tag management, and lightweight automation for large public-facing Drupal properties.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; keep them in one place or vary this section to only tools not named elsewhere.
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills overlaps with GitHub Actions; avoid repeating both without added specificity.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. Since “workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more implementation-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, not just brand names: “Workflow automation & work management: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; Slack, Teams.”
- Put strongest/most relevant tools first: lead with Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier if those were used to build actual systems.
- Consider adding light context if format allows: “used for editorial planning, approvals, cross-team coordination, and automated notifications.”
- Drop weaker/commodity tools if space is tight; keep only platforms tied to systems you designed or managed.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills, so avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack and Teams are common collaboration tools; listing both may add little unless central to workflow design.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, especially given the recent email leadership in NACo roles, but it’s currently just a vendor list. It would be stronger if framed around capability and aligned to the scale already shown elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform naming for readability: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show applied use, e.g. **newsletter operations, audience segmentation, campaign deployment**
- Optional stronger version: **Email marketing & engagement platforms: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys, Higher Logic, Mailchimp**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” and NACo bullets about newsletters; keep this item platform-focused rather than repeating email audience scale.
- If Dynamics 365 was not used recently or materially, consider dropping it to prioritize the most relevant/current systems.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool set, but this item is currently a generic list and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In a technical section, tighten it to tools/methods only and make the wording more precise.

Suggested edit
- Replace with: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI reporting dashboards**
- Swap **SEO** for **Google Search Console** or **SEO analysis**; “SEO” is too broad compared with the other tool-based entries.
- Change **Dashboarding** to **KPI reporting dashboards** or **executive dashboards** for clearer business value.
- If space allows elsewhere, move impact to experience bullets instead of here (e.g., analytics stack expansion, reporting improvements, decision support).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This nearly duplicates **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider keeping the Topline version outcome-focused and this one strictly tool-based.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating explanatory phrasing here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational: emphasize team-building, early platform/content ownership, and any scale or output metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground progression and first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving coordination across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete scope/results where possible: website refresh size/traffic, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience reach, or workflow/time-saved impact.
- Tighten the second sentence to one or two specific contributions: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring livestream and weekly video content for member communications.”
- Replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with a stronger management verb if accurate: “mentored,” “supervised,” or “trained” a digital media associate.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/building the capability rather than expanding it.
- Avoid repeating generic workflow language already used in later NACo roles unless tied to a distinct early achievement.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the innovation/program support angle and keep the digital piece concise.

Suggested edit:
- Lead with scope and support function: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program development and policy priorities.”
- Keep multimedia as a secondary clause, not the headline, to avoid repeating later digital roles.
- Tighten phrasing and use stronger verbs: replace “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with “produced digital and multimedia materials for program and policy communications.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program development and policy priorities. Produced digital and multimedia materials for program and policy communications, and launched NACo’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting and production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production/multimedia” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager and Associate Communications Director entries.
- If no metrics exist for the podcast, keep it brief rather than overstating an older accomplishment.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads a bit dated and overlaps with stronger multimedia claims already established in recent roles and Topline Skills. Tightening it to software/tools only will make it cleaner and less repetitive.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as tool proficiency rather than capabilities: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator”
- Replace broad workflow phrases with more specific tools or formats if available, e.g. “Livestream production” only if no platform names can be added.
- If podcast work is important, make it outcome-oriented elsewhere in experience; here, shorten to “Podcast editing/production” or remove it.
